skill.name: archify
skill.description: Create validated architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams as interactive HTML with SVG and export options. Use natural-language requirements, Mermaid input, or verified repository evidence.
skill.summary: Turn technical systems and processes into validated, interactive diagrams.
skill.author: tt-a1i

security_audit.summary: Adjudication dismissed 394 of 400 presented matches as test fixtures, generated data, documentation, or bounded local tooling. Six confirmed URLs cause generated artifacts or the update workflow to contact remote hosts, and semantic review found that the updater runs automatically without prior disclosure. Static presentation was capped at 400 of 8,055 matches, so 7,655 unpresented matches require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/8055 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 7655 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Generated HTML contacts Google Fonts when opened.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the required font files inside each artifact or use a system font stack with no external stylesheet or preconnect.

remediation.issue: The skill requires an update check without prior disclosure and hides check failures.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before the first network check, disclose the endpoint and cache path, and report failures without blocking diagram work.

content.value_statement: Complex systems are difficult to explain with text alone. Archify creates validated, interactive diagrams from requirements, Mermaid, or repository evidence.
actual_capabilities: Creates architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams.
Converts natural-language requirements and supported Mermaid structures into fresh diagram specifications.
Validates diagram schemas, geometry, composition, and delivery receipts.
Produces standalone HTML with inline SVG, themes, search, pan, zoom, and relationship tracing.
Exports diagrams as PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, or WebM artifacts.
Verifies architecture evidence against a pinned commit in a matching local Git repository.
limitations: Generation and validation require a local Node.js runtime and filesystem access.
Browser evidence and visual exports require a compatible local Chrome installation.
Viewer interface localization supports English and Simplified Chinese; other authored languages use English interface text.
Repository evidence supports architecture diagrams and requires a matching local Git checkout with a pinned commit.

use_cases.title: Document a Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Map runtime components, trust boundaries, dependencies, and the primary request path for engineering documentation.

use_cases.title: Explain an Operational Workflow
use_cases.description: Show owners, decisions, approvals, failure paths, and rollback steps in a readable process diagram.

use_cases.title: Trace Data and API Behavior
use_cases.description: Visualize message order, asynchronous work, data transformations, storage, lineage, and downstream consumers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture diagram for [system]. Show users, core services, storage, external dependencies, and the primary request path.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a concise system overview.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Mermaid
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Mermaid [flowchart, sequenceDiagram, or stateDiagram] into a polished Archify diagram: [paste Mermaid]. Preserve meaning and labels.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow for [process]. Separate owners into lanes and show approvals, blocking checks, failure handling, rollback, and recovery verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Document an operational or delivery process.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence-Based Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [repository path] and create an architecture diagram pinned to [commit]. Cite source evidence and mark every unsupported fact as unknown.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an advanced architecture backed by repository evidence.

output_examples.input: Show a web application with a browser, API, cache, database, queue, worker, and monitoring service.
output_examples.output: An interactive architecture artifact with trust boundaries, a clear request path, labeled asynchronous work, validation results, and delivery receipts.

output_examples.input: Explain a cache-miss request from the client through authentication, storage fallback, response, and asynchronous tracing.
output_examples.output: A sequence diagram with ordered participants, calls, returns, fallback behavior, and the tracing side effect.

output_examples.input: Map an analytics pipeline from collection through transformation, warehouse storage, governance, and reporting.
output_examples.output: A data-flow diagram with named datasets, transformations, ownership boundaries, storage stages, and downstream consumers.

best_practices: Provide exact component names, boundaries, protocols, and known failure paths.
Start with one primary path and add only details that improve understanding.
Validate after each focused correction and deliver only after all required checks pass.
anti_patterns: Do not invent repository facts, ownership, regions, protocols, or security boundaries.
Do not add manual routing controls before diagnostics identify a geometry problem.
Do not claim visual quality from automated checks without an actual visual review.

faq.question: Which diagram types are supported?
faq.answer: Archify supports architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams.

faq.question: Can it convert Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads supported Mermaid topology and meaning, then creates a fresh Archify specification.

faq.question: What output does it create?
faq.answer: It creates interactive HTML with inline SVG and can export PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, and WebM.

faq.question: Can it use repository evidence?
faq.answer: Yes, for architecture diagrams with a matching local Git checkout and a pinned public GitHub commit.

faq.question: Does validation replace visual review?
faq.answer: No. Validation checks objective contracts, while perceptual quality still requires a human or image-capable reviewer.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Core rendering is local, but update checks, remote brand capture, and external web fonts can make network requests.
